A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TDKPS research, with matching authors, framework, simulations, and digital-congressperson application. Their text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation results on power and false-positive rates, plus analyses of 99 digital congresspersons across 14 timepoints (Figures 3–6).

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical investigations and adds calibrated-test, signal-sparsity, embedding-model, retrieval-depth, and retrieval-quality results.

M1.justification: Appendix B.1.1 adds TDKPS-C, which splits response replicates into independent basis-estimation and testing subsets and permutes only the testing subset. This is a genuine but localized procedural extension; the joint embedding framework and paired-energy group test remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendices A.3.2 and B.1.2 add synthetic scenarios where temporal change affects only a subset of queries, extending evaluation from broadly distributed changes to sparse behavioral shifts. The real population, three query topics, and 2018–2024 coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 3 adds TDKPS-C to the comparisons, while its agent-count panel removes the oracle and DCorr curves shown in v1. Appendix D.3 introduces a random-tweet retrieval baseline. The existing group-level comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Added experiments introduce null-versus-alternative calibration comparisons, sparse-query designs with fixed or increasing total signal, and 200-permutation testing protocols. Appendix D evaluates four embedding configurations and retrieval depths of one to three tweets using rank agreement and retrieval-similarity measurements. These substantially expand evaluation design without establishing revisions to the original experiments' settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds calibration-versus-power analyses, separates signal sparsity from total signal strength, tests embedding-model and retrieval-depth sensitivity, evaluates retrieval against random tweets, and presents a query–tweet–response case study. These address several methodological and application-level questions absent from v1.

E5.justification: Beyond v1's trial counts and confidence bands, v2 reports standard errors from 100 Monte Carlo trials for calibration and 50 trials for sparsity (Tables 1–3). Retrieval quality also gains median and interquartile summaries. These are reporting additions for new analyses, not evidence of increased runs for the original experiments.

E6.justification: Figure 3 and Tables 1–3 add calibrated-test outcomes and sparse-signal findings. Tables 5–7 report embedding agreement of 0.992–0.998, retrieval-depth agreement of 0.812–0.874, and retrieval-quality differences. Figure 6B also changes existing results: Democrats' correlation changes from K=0.43, p=0.043 to K=0.51, p=0.017. The accompanying text retains the earlier values, creating an inconsistency.

T1.justification: The embedding objective, original hypotheses and test formulas, SNR arguments, and complexity derivations are retained. The sample-splitting extension reuses the distance statistic and permutation p-value formula; its calibration explanation is qualitative. Formal error guarantees remain future work.

C1.justification: The central embedding and agent/group monitoring contributions remain. Section 4 additionally makes identification of aggregate causal effects through query design and natural experiments an explicit framework-level conclusion. Since v1 already argued for a causal interpretation of its pandemic findings, this is a limited extension.

C2.justification: v2 distinguishes detecting behavioral change from identifying its responsible component and explicitly discusses inflated false-positive rates in the retained real-data analysis. It adds interpretations of signal concentration and pipeline sensitivity, explains the latent interactions behind tweet histories, and distinguishes expected stateful drift from anomalous or consequential change.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link advertised as providing code, data, and replication scripts, and specifies cosine similarity as the existing retrieval criterion. It also documents new simulation parameters and embedding-model names, dimensions, and sources. The original prompts, hardware, and generation-time disclosures remain.

R1.justification: Appendices A.3 and A.4 replace the Zhu and Ghodsi (2019) citation with the already cited 2006 scree-plot paper, and the separate 2019 reference disappears. The broader related-work positioning is retained; other reference changes primarily correct bibliographic metadata.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized terminology and wording edits, expands the application explanation and discussion, and adds an Impact Statement and appendix subsections. Most existing prose and the overall narrative order remain; scientific additions account for much of the document's growth.

P2.justification: Seven new tables introduce calibration, sparsity, configuration, correlation, and retrieval-quality displays. Figure 3 is redrawn with calibrated-test curves, an expanded legend, and altered proportions. Figure 6 changes labels and its caption and removes numerical vertical-axis ticks from panel C. The other principal figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's acknowledged false-positive inflation by implementing and evaluating a calibrated alternative. Table 1 demonstrates near-nominal rejection rates with an explicit power tradeoff, while the new robustness analyses strengthen the evidence supporting the pipeline. These gains outweigh the reporting inconsistency introduced between Figure 6 and its text. Calibration still costs power, and the retained real-data analysis remains uncalibrated; the improvement does not establish general error guarantees or causal identification.
